subject: Geography
description: Eight major soil types of India — distribution, characteristics, suitable crops

questions.stem: The most widely distributed soil in India by area is:
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil — covers ~46% of India's total area. Found in the Indo-Gangetic plain, brahmaputra valley, coastal belts of east coast (deltas of Mahanadi, Krishna, Godavari, Kaveri), Narmada and Tapi valleys. Two sub-types: Khadar (newer alluvium, fine-grained, fertile, replenished annually by floods) and Bhangar (older alluvium, contains kankar/calcareous nodules). Highly fertile — supports rice, wheat, sugarcane, oilseeds, pulses. Black soil is 2nd most extensive (~16%).

questions.stem: Black soil (Regur) is best suited for the cultivation of:

options.option_text: Cotton — hence also called 'black cotton soil'

questions.explanation: Black soil — formed from weathering of Deccan Trap basalts. Rich in iron, magnesium, lime, alumina; deficient in nitrogen, phosphorus, organic matter. Found in Maharashtra, MP, Gujarat (Saurashtra), parts of TN, AP, Karnataka. High moisture-retention capacity due to clayey texture (>50% clay). Develops cracks in summer = self-ploughing. Best for cotton, also good for jowar, wheat, sugarcane, oilseeds, citrus. Trap option Tea — actually grown on red/laterite soils; Coffee — laterite/red soils.

questions.stem: Laterite soil — typical of high-rainfall plateau regions — gets its red colour from:
questions.explanation: Laterite forms in tropical regions with high rainfall — silica leaches out leaving Fe and Al oxides. Fe oxide → red/brick colour ('latericius' = brick in Latin). Found in Western Ghats (Kerala, Karnataka, Goa), Eastern Ghats (Odisha), parts of Assam, Meghalaya, Chhattisgarh. Generally infertile (low N, P, K), acidic; useful for cashew, rubber, coffee, tea, coconut. Hardens on exposure → used as building bricks. Same root word 'laterite' derives.

questions.stem: Match the soil type with its dominant region — which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Arid / desert soil is found in RAJASTHAN (Thar desert), Haryana's southern parts, Gujarat's Kutch — NOT Punjab plains (which have rich alluvial soil from Indus tributaries). Desert soils are sandy, low in clay/humus, alkaline, saline; need irrigation + nitrogen. Indira Gandhi Canal has converted parts of western Rajasthan into productive agricultural land. Other major Indian soil types — peaty/marshy (Kerala backwaters, Sundarbans), forest soil (humus-rich on hills), saline-alkaline (Reh — UP, Haryana, dryland Maharashtra).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Khadar and Bhangar are sub-types of which soil?
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil — divided by AGE: Khadar = newer alluvium (light-coloured, fine-grained, more fertile, replenished by annual floods, found close to rivers); Bhangar = older alluvium (darker, coarser, contains 'kankar' calcareous nodules, often raised above flood-plains, less fertile but well-drained). Khadar suits intensive cultivation; Bhangar is good for plantation / construction. Term Bhangar comes from 'bhang' meaning broken / weathered.

questions.stem: Soil erosion in India is most severe in which form?
questions.explanation: Water erosion — main culprit (~75% of erosion-affected area in India). Forms: sheet (uniform thin layer removal), rill (small channels), gully (deep channels — Chambal-Yamuna ravines famous), riverbank, coastal. Wind erosion mostly in Rajasthan/Gujarat (~25% of total). Total degraded land in India ~30% (ICAR-IISWC). Mitigation — afforestation, contour bunding, terrace farming, gully plugging, check dams, mulching. Watershed development is the integrated approach.

questions.stem: ICAR's National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land-Use Planning (NBSS&LUP) is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: NBSS&LUP — Nagpur, Maharashtra. Established 1976 under ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research). Mandate — soil surveys at various scales (1:1M for India, district-level), classification, mapping (Soil Resource Maps of India), land-use planning. Issues 'Soil Health Card' jointly with state agriculture departments. India also has the Soil Health Card scheme (launched 2015 by PM Modi) — every farmer gets a card with soil-test results + recommendations every 2 years.
